$note: Single source for every number in spec §5.6 (R5.7). Generated by measuring commit 3176725 (main, tip of Wave 2 — 'docs: Wave 2 gate browser flows recorded') with scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs's own method, then hand-tightened. Do not hand-write a number here without re-running the measurement; the whole point of this gate is that it reflects a real build, not the spec's provisional table.
method: docs/research/v2/codebase-audit.md §3: read each route's .next/server/app/**/page_client-reference-manifest.js, resolve its entryJSFiles list against on-disk .next/static/chunks/*.js sizes, sum uncompressed bytes.
rules: (a) no route's budgetBytes may exceed its v1Bytes, ever, even when the measured tree is currently over budget.

(b) every route whose measured size exceeds specTargetBytes (the spec §5.6 direction) carries a named row in `ledger` saying which library is responsible and whether it is split, deferred, or accepted.

public.measuredNote: git ls-files public, uncompressed. 9 tracked files measured at 1,377,734 bytes (~1.3 MB) on 2026-09-07: two Java notices, two tree-sitter wasm, sql-wasm.wasm, and the sound sprite (CREDITS.md, brogram.json/.mp3/.webm) that landed with T0.5 after the spec's C1 correction was written (that correction counted 6 tracked files; the sound sprite adds 3 more).

ledger.library: src/lib/agents/buddy.ts (zod + the DeepSeek agent-request/response schemas), pulled into the client bundle by src/components/buddy/state.ts's plain `import { REFUSAL } from '@/lib/agents/buddy'`
ledger.note: This is not one of the spec's anticipated overages — it is a real bug found by this measurement, present identically on all 12 authenticated routes. Before the fix, one 475,150-byte chunk carries the leak (confirmed by content: it has zod's `ZodObject`/`ZodString` exports and the literal string "deepseek"); state.ts wants only the REFUSAL string constant, but a non-type-only import of one export from an agent module pulls the whole module — zod included — into every route that renders the buddy widget in the shell (today, every authenticated route). Verified directly: patching state.ts in a disposable worktree to hold its own copy of the REFUSAL string instead of importing it, then rebuilding, drops every route by exactly 375,465 bytes (confirmed identical across all 12 routes) — Turbopack re-packs the remaining ~99,685 bytes of that chunk (the buddy widget's own legitimate code) into a smaller, separate chunk rather than deleting it outright, so 375,465 bytes — not the full 475,150-byte chunk — is the true, fixable cost. Fix: move REFUSAL into a client-safe module with no zod import (or re-export it from a `'use client'`-safe barrel that never imports the agent files), not read from src/lib/agents/buddy.ts on the client. Out of T3.1's ownership (src/components/buddy/** belongs to T2.11) — reported and verified rather than fixed here. Every budgetBytes value above already excludes this 375,465 bytes (i.e. assumes the fix lands), so perf:bundle fails on the current tree until it does; that failure is the gate correctly biting on a genuine, newly measured regression, not a bug in this script.

Measured as one 231,786-byte chunk (confirmed: supabase/auth-js, supabase/ssr, supabase/gotrue-js strings), not the spec's guessed '~467 KB Supabase client pair' — that guess was wrong once actually measured (the real number is roughly half). This chunk already shipped in v1 (the audit's own '/dashboard' breakdown lists 'supabase 226'), so it is pre-existing cost, not new v2 weight. No ruling in the spec touches it; accepted as the cost of an authenticated route with no server-fetched page data. Splitting it further (e.g. lazier auth-js import) is not scheduled for v2.

ledger.library: the buddy widget's own code (~97 KB, legitimate) + @tanstack/react-query + motion + gsap + next-themes + the sound manager + AppShell/ShellLayout/WellnessSlot chrome
ledger.note: Measured on the same leak-fixed rebuild used to verify the row above: /dashboard's fixed total is 809,046 bytes; subtracting the 231,786-byte Supabase pair leaves 577,260 bytes, most of it framework/layout chunks Next.js always ships plus the shell libraries this wave added. This is the shell weight §5.6's own critique predicted ('realistically pushes it back toward 550-600 KB'); measured reality lands close to that guess. Accepted for v2 launch; a future task can dynamic-import next-themes' non-critical pieces or gate GSAP behind first-gesture the way the sound sprite already is (§7.7) if this needs to shrink further.

Not part of the /exercise/[id] budget above at all — it never appears in entryJSFiles because Editor.tsx is next/dynamic({ ssr: false }) (spec §5.5), so it loads only once the editor mounts. Measured directly from the built react-loadable-manifest and per-language chunk fingerprints on this same tree, replacing the spec's '~400-500 KB, not measured' estimate: the always-loaded Editor bundle (basicSetup + @codemirror/state + @codemirror/view + Editor.tsx itself) is ~395 KB (404,666 bytes across its 4 chunk files); the one grammar the exercise's language actually needs adds ~70 KB for Python (the lightest launch-course grammar, 71,808 bytes) up to ~139 KB for JavaScript/TypeScript/Mongo (142,317 bytes across 2 chunk files) or ~57 KB for SQL (58,788 bytes) on top of that — a single-grammar 'cold' editor load of roughly 465-535 KB, well under the audit's original monolithic all-five-grammars chunk (658 KB, shipped on every exercise regardless of language).

Not gated by this script — the gate above asserts tracked public/ only (git ls-files public), which never includes tools.jar (gitignored). tools.jar is fetched at build by `npm run prepare:java` and served same-origin, which the CheerpJ ruling (spec §3 C1) requires: Java is live (NEXT_PUBLIC_JUDGE_PROVIDER=browser), so a permanent 3 MB deploy cap and a shipped Java adapter cannot both be true. The plan's choice: keep tools.jar out of git and out of this gate, and carry its ~17.5 MB (measured: 18,361,919 bytes, sha256-verified at fetch time) as this named, permanent, accepted deploy-time cost instead of a CI assertion no build can pass while Java stays live.
